Drinking a hot beverage to cool yourself works on the principle of evaporation. You make yourself warmer, which causes your body to sweat more. The more you sweat, the more fluid that can be evaporated off your body, which makes you feel cooler.

This is also how a fan makes you feel cooler; even though you're blowing warm air over yourself, it aids the evaporation process which cools you down. The hot beverage "trick" requires that the sweat can evaporate off you, which doesn't work as well when it's already humid. You could try this and directing a fan to blow over you, to get the "best of both worlds."

In regards to a shower... if you have the ability to cool your body with cold water, this will be more effective than trying to use sweat evaporation. You have to cool your body enough to where you feel cold, but without shivering (as this is how the body heats itself up). Then you'll feel more comfortable outside the shower. as you'll be cool and not "sticky" feeling. As you warm back up, your body will sweat as it needs to. Once you feel "sticky" again or uncomfortable, just repeat.

The hot tea in the Sahara principle is bunk. You're raising your core body temperature by drinking something hot, which overexerts your body into trying to cool itself off when it's already expending a good deal energy toward that. There are people who swear by this approach to coping with the heat but they tend to be people who are pretty superstitious anyway, a.e. not prone to making rational assessments of the world.

I lived in Vegas for 12 years. If you need to go outside for a longer time when it's hot out, wear long sleeves. Wear full trousers. Wear a hat. Douse yourself. you'll dry off in about 15 minutes. Do it again. Repeat until your outside task is done.

Always carry water with you.

Inside you can splash water on yourself every several minutes and it should help a lot. make sure to stay hydrated.

Get low, on the ground. Find tile or non-carpeted floor. Lay with as few clothes on as possible so your skin will be against the floor.

Use a box fan and a revolving fan on you.
When I was without air conditioning, I would fill empty 2-liter soda bottles with water and freeze them. Rotate a couple of them at a time in front of a fan, and enjoy the coolness as they thaw
